chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man who said, 'Hamza ibn Humran narrated to me saying, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

'Whenever one of you intends goodness, let him not delay it, for the servant sometimes prays the prayer or fasts the day, and it is said to him: Do whatever you wish after it, for Allah has forgiven you.'
ai.seo_question: Why should one hasten to perform good deeds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) encourages believers to hasten in performing good deeds, explaining that after performing a prayer or fasting a day, a person may be granted permission to indulge in permissible desires, as Allah has forgiven their sins for that act of worship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Numan who said, 
‘Hamza Bin Humran narrated to me saying, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying:

‘Whenever one of you intends the goodness, so he should not delay it, for the servant sometimes prays the Salāt or Fasts for the day, and it is said to him: ‘Do whatever you so desire to after it, for Allahazwj has Forgiven (your sins) for you’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Nu’man who has that narrated to him Hamzah ibn Humran who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying,

‘When one of you intends to do a good deed, he should do it without delay; a servant (of Allah) perhaps performs a prayer or fasts for a day, thereupon, it is said to him, “Do whatever you like (other good deeds) after this act, Allah has already granted you forgiveness. (One may not know which of his worships has been accepted.)”’
